Existing physics-augmented pipelines simulate rigid bodies only and cannot accommodate a generated deformable object, which text-to-3D generation returns as a geometrically invalid mesh, sometimes self-intersecting, that has no rest shape, no material model and no admissible initial state. These are the inputs a deformable simulation requires, and we construct each from information already in the pipeline. The rest shape comes from how the object is manufactured rather than from the generated physically inconsistent deformed configuration, and a material library assigns each deformable object its initial elastic parameters, which can then be optimized. The occluded support is regenerated and converted into a watertight collision mesh, each object is released from an optimizable placement above the supporting part that the prompt specifies, and the complete scene is driven to static equilibrium under one unified contact model, with completion verified by geometric checks and a vision-language model. When a scene fails the prompt, a grid search over placements corrects it, and the adjoint of a differentiable simulation of the same contact energy reaches the targets the grid does not, places several bodies jointly and recovers and optimizes material parameters. Multi-body scenes equilibrate in a single simulation, and the pipeline also runs from the text prompt alone. On all sixty-five prompts, SoftPAT3D produces no undesired interpenetration of any kind, whereas every other system does, and its scenes directly support scene editing and robotic manipulation.

Human-Computer Interaction.title: Exploring Mixed-Reality for Enhancing Driver Warning Systems: A Preliminary Study on Attention-Shifting Methods and Hazard Perception
Human-Computer Interaction.summary: Modern vehicles are equipped with advanced sensors and capabilities, yet engaging human drivers effectively in hazard perception remains a challenging research area. This paper investigates the potential of mixed reality (MR) to enhance driver warning systems. The study examines the impact of attention-shifting methods, including visual cues, audio cues, and a combination of both, on drivers' hazard perception. A preliminary study involving six participants was conducted, and the NASA-TLX analysis did not yield significant differences. However, through the use of functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS), we unveil distinct brain activation patterns associated with visual and sound cues. Further research with larger sample sizes and diverse driving scenarios is required to validate and expand upon these preliminary results.
Human-Computer Interaction.comment: 8 pages, 3 figures

Human-Computer Interaction.title: Feel My Focus: Gaze-Triggered Digital Twin Creation for Remote Collaboration
Human-Computer Interaction.summary: We present Feel My Focus, a gaze-triggered mixed reality (MR) demonstration that enables rapid creation and sharing of lightweight 3D digital twins during remote collaboration. Unlike systems that use gaze primarily as a referential pointer, Feel My Focus treats sustained visual attention as a generative action: a fixation on a physical object initiates single-image capture, attention-guided segmentation, and one-shot 3D reconstruction, allowing a remote partner to inspect and discuss the object in situ. The system integrates gaze-tracking glasses, modular segmentation and reconstruction services, and an MR client for runtime streaming and interaction. This design prioritizes responsiveness and experiential continuity over photometric fidelity. We report observations from a public demonstration, highlighting design trade-offs, failure modes, and user control considerations for deploying gaze-triggered generative systems in real-world collaborative settings.
Human-Computer Interaction.comment: 5 pages, 3 figures

Human-Computer Interaction.title: Trail Making Tests in Extended Reality: A Critical Review with Implications for Cognitive Ageing
Human-Computer Interaction.summary: Extended reality (XR) versions of the Trail Making Test and Color Trails Test are promising for assessing and training cognition in older adults. However, each XR adaptation is a new instrument, whose display, interaction technique, timing rules and layouts may change what it measures. This critical narrative review maps these implementations by software lineage and appraises their evidence for assessment and training against common criteria. The Trail Making Test in Virtual Reality (TMT-VR), whose source code was inspected, serves as a measurement case. XR trail-making tests showed convergence with paper and computerised versions, varying by test part and sample, and clinical group differences (e.g., Parkinson's disease, mild cognitive impairment). However, gaps in reliability (e.g., randomised forms), validation (e.g., norms, prospective samples) and reporting (e.g., error handling, build identity) emerged, and no training benefit attributable to the trail-making component was identified. The TMT-VR case shows how interaction technique, timing rule, error handling and unlogged layouts shape a score's meaning. Future tests should log layouts and events, estimate alternate-form reliability and undergo prospective validation, and training trials should isolate the trail-making component. Several XR trail-making tests have moved beyond feasibility, and reported tolerability during supervised sessions supports further evaluation in older adults.
Human-Computer Interaction.comment: Review article. 22 pages, 1 figure, 4 tables; Supplementary Materials (19 pages); ancillary files: the Supplementary Materials (PDF), File S1 (evidence map, XLSX and CSV) and File S2 (XR inventory, XLSX)

The prototype uses the \$1 Unistroke Recognizer to map gestures to symbols and translates their locations and sizes into tensor-field attractors and weighted parameter grids. Implemented in JavaScript and TypeScript with React and Three.js, the prototype supports interactive sketching, visualization, and urban massing generation. Human-Computer Interaction.title: Dashboard Remixing: Goal-oriented Organization and Enrichment of Visualizations and Insights
Human-Computer Interaction.summary: Dashboard creation requires iteratively authoring multiple views and organizing them into a structured format. However, creators often struggle to step back and assess their own work for organization and refinement due to cognitive limitations. In this work, we propose a pipeline to provide computational support for self-reflection during the design process. Our pipeline automatically infers analytical objectives, discovers implicit patterns, and structures those patterns to surface coherent analytical pathways. It further enriches existing dashboard designs by generating complementary visualizations and aggregating natural language insights based on relationships across data entities (e.g., contrasting, drill-down, and relatedness) to reveal chart connections. Our rule-based pipeline provides objective, verifiable feedback, offering an external perspective while enabling creators to tell their own data stories. Four case studies and six expert interviews demonstrate how this approach helps creators reflect on organizational alternatives and surface hidden analytical opportunities in a principled way, reducing the cognitive burden while encouraging deeper analytical exploration.

Human-Computer Interaction.title: From MNH to the Friedman--Komogortsev Method---which changes improve eye-movement classification?
Human-Computer Interaction.summary: The Friedman-Komogortsev Method (FKM) is a rule-based classifier of fixations, saccades, and post-saccadic oscillations in 1000-Hz recordings, developed from the modified Nyström-Holmqvist algorithm (MNH) and used in several recent studies. FKM changes MNH in many ways at once: it centres MNH's Savitzky-Golay filter, adds a position-based test for whether an apparent post-saccadic oscillation continues the saccade, adds rejection tests, and changes several thresholds. We asked which of these changes alter agreement with human classification. Both algorithms were scored against twenty 26-s GazeBase reading recordings hand-classified by three trained raters, and each change was reverted in turn. FKM agreed better than MNH as MNH was used: saccade Cohen's kappa rose on all 20 recordings (median +0.034), and saccade boundaries moved from 2-3 ms late to the raters' sample. One change produced this: centring the filter, which removes a three-sample delay. Reinstating the delay returned FKM's saccade kappa to MNH's value, and centring MNH's filter alone made MNH match FKM on saccades and exceed it on post-saccadic events. The position-based test changed how saccades with several velocity peaks were divided, splitting 8% of rater-labelled "wavy" saccades into a saccade and a spurious oscillation against 39% for delay-corrected MNH. FKM's higher post-saccadic velocity floor traded recall for precision. The remaining changes had no measurable effect on these recordings. FKM's improvement over MNH is therefore a filter-alignment correction that MNH users can apply directly, plus a segmentation rule for multi-peak saccades.
Human-Computer Interaction.comment: The details about the classification is described in the supplementary materials

Human-Computer Interaction.title: Facilitating the Integration of LLMs Into Online Experiments With Simple Chat
Human-Computer Interaction.summary: As large language models (LLMs) become increasingly prevalent, understanding human-LLM interactions is emerging as a central priority in psychological research. Online experiments offer an efficient means to study human-LLM interactions, yet integrating LLMs into established survey platforms remains technically demanding, particularly when aiming for ecologically realistic, real-time conversational experiences with strong experimental control. We introduce Simple Chat, an open-source, research-focused chat interface that streamlines LLM integration for platforms such as Qualtrics, oTree, and LimeSurvey, while presenting a unified participant experience across conditions. Simple Chat connects to both commercial providers and open-weights models, displays streamed responses incrementally, and offers an administrative interface for fine-grained control of prompts and interface features. Simple Chat is available both as a hosted service that requires no installation and as open-source software that researchers can deploy on their own server or adapt to their needs. By reducing technical barriers and standardizing interfaces, Simple Chat helps advance the study of human-LLM interaction. In this article, we outline Simple Chat's key features, provide a step-by-step tutorial, and demonstrate its utility through two illustrative case studies.
Human-Computer Interaction.comment: Revised version

Human-Computer Interaction.title: From Dialogue to Task: How Cognitive Engagement With Generative Artificial Intelligence Relates to Post-Dialogue Activity and Task Outcomes
Human-Computer Interaction.summary: Generative AI is increasingly embedded within learning tasks, yet interaction frequency reveals little about cognitive engagement in student-AI dialogue. Little is known about how such engagement is situated within task workflows or how dialogue characteristics and subsequent task activity relate to students' behaviour and task outcomes. This study examined cognitive engagement in student-AI dialogue, its position within task workflows, and associations of dialogue and task-process characteristics with post-dialogue activity and task outcomes. Data were collected from 1,681 students across 40 university courses using three AI companions embedded in resource creation, peer moderation, and practice. Cognitive engagement in 829 conversation threads was coded with a dialogue-oriented Interactive-Constructive-Active-Passive (ICAP) framework, and 2,969 task sequences were modelled with first-order Markov models. Regression models linked dialogue and task-process characteristics to behavioural re-engagement, peer-rated artefact quality, and practice performance. Passive and Active engagement predominated, although resource creation involved more Constructive and Interactive dialogue, peer moderation more Passive, and practice more Active, while higher-engagement dialogue was less often followed by session termination. In resource creation, student-composed messages were associated with more dialogue-to-task returns than template-only requests at the same Passive level, whereas deeper cognitive engagement was associated with higher final artefact quality independent of return frequency; in practice, AI dialogue after an incorrect attempt was associated with fewer further attempts but higher next-attempt correctness among continuers. Post-dialogue activity and task outcomes are distinct aspects of AI use that interaction frequency cannot capture and evaluations should assess separately.
Human-Computer Interaction.comment: 31 pages, 12 figures. Submitted to the Journal of Computer Assisted Learning

Human-Computer Interaction.title: Linking Event-sequence Data Claims to Analytic Provenance in Chatbots: Technique and Evaluation
Human-Computer Interaction.summary: Chatbots are increasingly used to analyze temporal event sequences of which website clickstreams are among the most common. Explanations are essential for understanding claims about event-sequence data. However, existing systems often require programming expertise to interpret these explanations and fail to explain the data processes underlying the data claims. We introduce a technique for linking a data claim to its analytic provenance (i.e., the analytic steps and results that produced it). It has two components: a reference table that records analytic steps and results in addressable cells, and a citation format that binds each claim to one or more cells. To operationalize this technique for clickstream analysis, we curated a set of analytic operations for clickstream analysis, organized them through a pivot-table abstraction, and developed tools that an AI agent can invoke to create a reference table and assemble a natural language response with cited data claims. To evaluate how citations affect users' assessment of data claims, we conducted two crowdsourced experiments with 90 participants each. The experiments showed that participants perceived correct data claims to be more accurate with citations when compared with no explanations, and that they perceived incorrect data claims to be less accurate with citations when compared with code and no explanations.

Human-Computer Interaction.title: CRAFT: Exploring Wearable Creative AI on Smart Glasses for Fiction Writing in Real-World Contexts
Human-Computer Interaction.summary: Creative writing increasingly integrates AI assistance, yet current tools miss in-situ moments when writers draw inspiration from real-world experiences. We envision Context-aware Reality-Fiction Transformation (CRAFT), an approach for AI glasses that translates daily experiences into fiction narratives. We explored its desirability, feasibility, and potential viability through three studies. Interviews with nine writers yielded desires and three design goals: 1) augmenting in-situ perception to bridge reality-fiction gaps, 2) promoting authenticity grounded in real-world experiences while maintaining fictionalization, and 3) preserving creative agency, enjoyment, and life-art boundaries. Co-design workshops with 16 writers and researchers operationalized these goals into concrete interaction mechanisms using a technology probe. We then conducted supported field trials with eight writers across 24 sessions using a refined probe, revealing writer-perceived benefits (e.g., enriched fictional ideas from serendipitous encounters), emergent practices (e.g., micro-creation), and design considerations for future sustained use. We contribute design explorations for the CRAFT approach, offering design implications and empirical insights on ubiquitous human-AI creative collaboration in everyday life.
Human-Computer Interaction.comment: Published in Proceedings of the ACM on Interactive, Mobile, Wearable and Ubiquitous Technologies (PACM IMWUT), Vol. 10, No. 3, Article 81, September 2026. This research was supported in part by the CityU Start-up Grant (No. 9610677) and the Research Grants Council of Hong Kong under the Early Career Scheme (Project No. 24612523)

Human-Computer Interaction.title: Who Benefits from Wikipedia's Growth Mentorship? The Role of Newcomer Information Needs
Human-Computer Interaction.summary: Evaluations of Wikipedia's programs for new editors usually ask whether a program works on average; we ask which newcomers benefit when their question to a mentor gets a reply. English Wikipedia's Growth mentorship system assigns every new account a volunteer mentor, and about a quarter of the questions newcomers send never get a reply. Using the first questions of 34,073 newcomers (2021 to 2026), we compare newcomers who received a reply with similar newcomers who did not, matched on 164 characteristics recorded before the question (propensity score stratification). (1) Does a reply help newcomers keep editing? Yes, in the short term: in the 14 days after the reply, newcomers who received one were 1.8 percentage points (pp) more likely to edit an article (22% vs. an estimated 20% without a reply) and 1.8pp more likely to edit on two or more days. Later in the first year, the only difference that remains significant after correction for multiple testing is in the share who edit an article at least once between six months and one year after the reply (+1.5pp). (2) Does the effect depend on what the newcomer asked? Yes. We sort questions by Morrison's (1993) information-seeking types, which earlier studies measured mostly through self-reports, using a language model checked against human labels. A reply has significant effects for questions about rules and norms (+3.4pp), questions that show the newcomer's earlier editing (+3.4pp) and specific how-to questions (+2.4pp). For newcomers who do not know what to work on, a reply has no detectable effect, and the effect is 4.2pp smaller than for newcomers with other questions. (3) Which replies are followed by more editing? Among newcomers who received a reply, those whose reply came sooner or stayed closer to the topic of their question edited more.
Human-Computer Interaction.comment: 25 pages, 10 figures. Accepted at ICWSM 2027

Human-Computer Interaction.title: Wording Matters: Understanding How GenAI Policy Rules Shape Teachers' and Students' Workflows and Perceptions
Human-Computer Interaction.summary: The growing use of generative AI (GenAI) in higher education has led institutions to develop policies governing its applications. However, we have little knowledge about how teachers and students adapt and adhere to the policies. In this paper, we analyzed GenAI policies from 101 U.S. universities, identifying nine recurring rules for GenAI use, and interviewed 20 students and 20 faculty members about the rules. We find that the wording of the rules can change how students perceive and act on the rules while introducing different challenges that teachers face in enforcing them in practice. For example, rules such as "Passing off AI-generated content as your own constitutes academic dishonesty" and "Students are accountable for any inaccurate, biased, or unethical content" both outline the acceptable use of AI, but the former can make students hide their use of AI out of fear of unwanted scrutiny, whereas the latter can encourage students to take responsibility and ownership of their use of AI and be more transparent. Students described uncertainty about acceptable use, fear of penalties and unfair treatment, and stigma that discouraged acknowledging AI use. Teachers took on approval workload, had to interpret acceptable use, and lacked reliable ways to verify compliance. We summarize these impacts in a policy-impact matrix linking each rule to its effects on teacher and student workflows and perception.

Human-Computer Interaction.title: GARP: Real-Time Generative Agents on Local Hardware in a Game Engine
Human-Computer Interaction.summary: Generative agents are game characters whose plans, conversations, and memories are written on the fly by a large language model (LLM). The original Generative Agents demonstration used cloud inference in a custom simulation. We present GARP, a platform for real-time generative agents inside Godot, and describe the Character Behavior System used in GARP 2. The complete loop runs on local hardware using a 3B-parameter open-weight model and no cloud service. Alongside the original planning, memory, and reflection, GARP gives each agent an emotion system driven by LLM appraisal, four graded personality axes drawn from the Big Five that set simulation parameters as well as prompt text, six needs whose urgency grows over time, and pairwise relationships updated after every conversation. The system narrows 50+ candidate actions to typically 3-8, constrains model responses with JSON schemas, and surfaces important memories in decision prompts. A layered optimization strategy (an adjustable game clock, decisions taken ahead of need, multi-tier caching, prompt compression, and fully asynchronous execution) keeps the game responsive while the model thinks. In a nine-scenario evaluation, 25 of 27 runs passed log-based checks. Both failures occurred in the birthday party scenario, where one guest omitted the event from their daily plan.
Human-Computer Interaction.comment: 13 pages, 13 figures

Human-Computer Interaction.title: Known Good, Known Bad: A Ground-Truth Calibration Protocol for AI Judgment in Science
Human-Computer Interaction.summary:
Scientific use of generative AI requires evaluation against cases with independently checkable answers. We present a ground truth calibration protocol that compares a verified reference case with reference deviant variants through neutral evaluation, an authority framed recheck, and a line by line audit. Human adjudication distinguishes deviation detection, premise accommodation, unsupported doubt, and correctness of the resulting calculation.
  An instructor generated organic chemistry demonstration comprises six conversations and 18 responses from an unidentified backend served through the free logged out ChatGPT interface in July 2026. Neutral evaluation detected three of five intended deviations. Both initial misses, involving oxidant stoichiometry and experimental scale, were detected at the authority framed second turn; all five detections persisted at the third turn audit. The fixed sequence supports a descriptive account of recovery across turns. In the scale case, the model initially produced a locally coherent peroxide limited yield. After recognizing the unit problem, it incorrectly retained that limiting reagent conclusion for the corrected scale. Detection and numerical repair therefore require separate assessment. The verified reference attracted speculative concerns while retaining its correct yield calculation.
  The protocol connects documentary verification of scientific claims and citations with empirical verification of laboratory interpretations. It supplies inspectable transcripts, reference calculations, behavior codes, and a reusable calibration architecture for AI literacy instruction. The pilot demonstrates the protocol's measures in one case family; replicated model evaluation and learner assessment are the next validation steps.
Human-Computer Interaction.comment: 18 pages, 3 figures, 6 tables

Systems and Control.title: Conditions for Normality of Pontryagin's Maximum Principle in the Absence of State Constraints
Systems and Control.summary: Pontryagin's Maximum Principle is said to be "normal" for the problem at hand when it has a solution (maximizer u*) that explicitly involves the problem's cost function, making the maximum principle helpful (while in the opposite situation it is of no help). The aim of the present paper is, for Lagrange optimal control problems without state constraints, to identify classes of problems for which the Principle is normal. General conditions are introduced that guarantee normality, and classes of problems that satisfy these conditions are identified. Such classes include problems for which the constrained (by bounds on the control values) "augmented" reachable set, with cost along an upward vertical axis, has a convex lower-boundary function and the optimal terminal state lies in the relative interior of the reachable state set, with the terminal constraint within the affine hull of that set. Such classes include problems for which the constrained (by bounds on the values of the control signal) "augmented" (with the cost value along an upward "vertical axis") reachable set has a "convex" lower boundary for which the optimal terminal state lies in the relative interior of the set of reachable states. Special attention is given to Lagrange steering problems: sufficient conditions are obtained on a nested sequence of sub-classes of such problems, culminating with the class of steering problems with scalar control signal and linear time-invariant (LTI) state dynamics and objective integrand, for which normality is guaranteed whenever all eigenvalues of the state dynamics matrix A are real (e.g., if A is symmetric or triangular or the system is overdamped) or have small enough imaginary parts; simple 2 x 2 examples show that, in contrast with the situation in the finite-dimensional case, this property does not extend to arbitrary A matrices.

Systems and Control.title: Digital Twin Networks for 6G Wireless Systems: Architecture, Enabling Technologies, AI-Driven Control, and Open Challenges
Systems and Control.summary: The transition to the Sixth Generation (6G) of mobile networks requires proactive and deterministic orchestration to satisfy the stringent key performance indicators of future services, including ultra-reliable low-latency communications, enhanced mobile broadband, and massive machine-type communications. Digital Twin Networks (DTNs) have emerged as a foundational technology to meet these demands, offering real-time and high-fidelity virtual replicas of the physical network. Although the literature explores DTNs conceptually, a gap exists in the coverage of technical classification and computational feasibility evaluations. This survey addresses this gap by formally categorizing state-of-the-art DTN architectures into passive monitoring twins and active control twins. We evaluate their enabling technologies, namely ray-tracing, reconfigurable intelligent surfaces, artificial intelligence, and multi-access edge computing. Importantly, we analyze the complexity of ten state-of-the-art frameworks, five reporting complexity expressions, four derived in this survey, and one not derivable, to assess hardware scalability and inference bottlenecks. These architectures are then linked to forthcoming 6G use cases, including smart cities, Industry 5.0, healthcare, and smart grids. Finally, we synthesize crucial unresolved challenges, highlighting graphics processing unit hardware limitations, cyber-physical actuation latency, and the need for a zero-trust security paradigm, offering research directions toward the unified Internet of Everything.

Systems and Control.title: Concurrent Learning-Based Inertial Parameter Estimation and Control of Quadrotors
Systems and Control.summary: In this letter, we consider trajectory tracking control and inertial parameter estimation of a quadrotor UAV whose center of mass (CoM) does not coincide with its geometric center. Onboard payloads like an IMU, a camera, or a battery are not necessarily placed at its geometric center. Moreover, during the flight these sensors might move because of external disturbances and cause a CoM offset. Thus, these events and equipment introduce an offset and cause the inertia matrix to be non-diagonal. We develop an integral concurrent learning (ICL)-based geometric controller that estimates the mass, the CoM offset, and the full inertia matrix online, without an accelerometer or numerical derivatives, and tracks a given trajectory corrected by the offset estimated online. We prove that the estimated parameters converge to their true values under a finite excitation condition. We validate the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm using a simulation example.
Systems and Control.comment: 6 pages, 4 figures. To be submitted to IEEE Control Systems Letters (L-CSS) with the CDC 2027 option

Systems and Control.title: All-Pass Function OPF: A Solver-Friendly, Physics-Preserving Approximation of AC OPF
Systems and Control.summary: This paper presents a rational approximation of the AC optimal power flow (AC OPF) problem based on an all-pass approximation of the exponential power flow kernel. The classical AC OPF relies on trigonometric coupling between bus voltage phasors, which yields a nonconvex program with oscillatory derivatives that can slow, or in some cases destabilize, interior-point methods. We replace the trigonometric terms with an all-pass function (APF) approximation whose real and imaginary components act as smooth surrogates for the cosine and sine functions, and we introduce a pre-rotation to shift the argument of the approximation toward its most accurate region, ensuring that the reformulated power flow model preserves physical loss behavior, maintains the symmetry of the classical kernels, and improves the conditioning of the Jacobian and Hessian matrices. The proposed APF OPF formulation remains nonconvex, as in the classical model, but it eliminates trigonometric evaluations and empirically produces larger and more stable Newton steps under standard interior-point solvers. Numerical results on more than 25 IEEE and PGLib test systems ranging from 9 to 10{,}000 buses demonstrate that the APF OPF model achieves solutions with accuracy comparable to that of the classical formulation while reducing solver times, indicating a more solver-friendly nonconvex representation of AC OPF. All code, functions, verification scripts, and generated results are publicly available on \href{https://github.com/LSU-RAISE-LAB/APF-OPF}{GitHub}, along with a README describing how to run and reproduce the experiments.

Systems and Control.title: Robust Adaptive Backup Control Barrier Functions
Systems and Control.summary: We propose a notion of robust adaptive backup control barrier functions for nonlinear control affine systems with parametric uncertainty in both the drift dynamics and actuation matrix. Backup control barrier functions guarantee safety by predicting the system's trajectory under a pre-certified safe controller. However, these predictions rely on the model and can be inaccurate when the system contains unknown parameters. To address this issue, we estimate the unknown parameters using element-wise certified adaptive estimators that provide a parameter adaptation law and component-wise estimation error bounds. We compute the backup flow using the estimated model and tighten the safety conditions using these certified bounds. The resulting safety conditions account for the sensitivity of the predicted flow to parameter estimation errors. Moreover, to handle uncertainty in the actuation matrix, we use a duality-based reformulation that enables the use of a computationally efficient quadratic-program-based safety filter. We prove that controllers satisfying the proposed robust adaptive backup control barrier function constraints guarantee safety under parametric uncertainty and input constraints.

Systems and Control.title: Ultrawideband Polarization-Rotating Antenna for Enhanced Ground Penetrating Radar Detection
Systems and Control.summary: Ground penetrating radar (GPR) represents a powerful and widely adopted tool for nondestructive subsurface detection and imaging. To overcome the impaired detection performance caused by polarization mismatch in conventional single-channel GPR systems, this paper presents an innovative ultrawideband polarization-rotating (UPR) antenna that achieves rotating linear polarizations (LPs) by varying the source frequency for enhanced detection. The developed UPR antenna achieves a continuous polarization rotation from $0^\circ$ to $170^\circ$ across 1.2 to 3.2 GHz, as verified by both full-wave simulations and experimental measurements. The antenna is subsequently integrated into a single-channel stepped-frequency GPR system and evaluated against targets of varying geometries in a sandy environment. Compared with a conventional fixed-LP GPR system, the UPR antenna-enabled GPR system delivers markedly more consistent detection performance across all target types, with particularly pronounced enhancements for polarization-sensitive targets. By enabling ultrawideband frequency-dependent polarization agility, the proposed GPR system enhances subsurface target detection while maintaining the simplicity and low cost of a single-channel measurement architecture.

Systems and Control.title: K-PWM: Control-Oriented Structured Bilinear World Models under Partial Observation
Systems and Control.summary: World models learn internal simulators of environment dynamics for prediction, planning, and control, yet learning them from limited, noisy, and partial observations remains challenging. While much progress has focused on pixel-based observations, many physical systems instead provide vector-valued measurements that reveal only part of the underlying state. We introduce K-PWM, a probabilistic world model for prediction and control under partial observation. K-PWM couples Koopman-bilinear latent dynamics with a nonlinear observation decoder and performs probabilistic latent-state inference through the learned model via extended Kalman filtering and smoothing, without a separately trained inference network. Its bilinear structure enables exact propagation of the maintained Gaussian belief through the latent transition and efficient rollouts for uncertainty-aware model predictive path integral (MPPI) control. For training K-PWM, we present a generalized expectation conditional maximization (GECM) procedure with closed-form updates for the generators, noise covariances, and latent prior, complemented by gradient-based decoder learning. A Koopman-consistent initialization selects the latent dimension from data and initializes the action-dependent dynamics. With limited training data, K-PWM achieves lower long-horizon prediction error than the evaluated baselines on partially observed Gymnasium MuJoCo systems, while substantially reducing training time relative to the strongest prediction baseline. On high-dimensional MuJoCo Menagerie robots, it achieves competitive tracking accuracy with low per-step computation times, demonstrating potential for real-time deployment. These results support structured probabilistic dynamics as a data- and compute-efficient approach to world modeling and control under partial observation.

Systems and Control.title: Pricing Short-Circuit Current via a Primal-Dual Formulation for Preserving Integrality Constraints
Systems and Control.summary: Synchronous Generators (SGs) currently provide important levels of Short-Circuit Current (SCC), a critical ancillary service that ensures line protections trip during short-circuit faults. Given the ongoing replacement of SGs by power-electronics-based generation, which has a hard limit on current injection, it has become relevant to optimize the procurement of SCC services provided by remaining SGs. Pricing this service, i.e., computing dual variables of SCC constraints, is however challenging due to the integrality constraints in Unit Commitment (UC). Existing methods, e.g., dispatchable pricing and restricted pricing, attempt to address this issue but exhibit limitations in handling non-convexities, resulting in SCC prices that either fail to cover the operating costs of units or lack interpretability. To overcome these pitfalls, we adopt a primal-dual formulation of the existing SCC-constrained dispatch that preserves the binary UC for effectively computing shadow prices of SCC services. Using a modified IEEE 30-bus system, the proposed method is compared with the previously developed pricing schemes. It is demonstrated that, under the proposed pricing method, revenue-adequate and explicit service prices can be assigned without the need for make-whole payments, an advantage that cannot be achieved by other pricing approaches.

Systems and Control.title: Pre-Solve Horizon Sampling of Frozen Acceleration Residuals for Quadrotor NMPC under External Forces
Systems and Control.summary: We investigate how a frozen supervised acceleration-residual model should be sampled within nonlinear model predictive control (NMPC) of a quadrotor subject to external forces. Cyclewise deployment holds the current-state residual across the prediction horizon, whereas stagewise deployment evaluates the same network at shifted warm-start nodes before each optimization solve. The correction sequence is fixed during optimization and the network is not updated online. In 220 simulated pulse-load conditions, cyclewise and stagewise deployment reduce mean integral absolute position error (IAE) relative to nominal NMPC by 4.38% and 7.77%, respectively. However, both worsen all 55 hover conditions, and most of the aggregate improvement arises after pulse removal rather than during loading. In 96 prescribed random-force blocks, stagewise deployment reduces mean IAE by 11.99%; the evaluated finite-budget reinforcement-learning add-ons do not improve their matched supervised means in either force bank. A separate causal innovation compensator reduces mean IAE by 27.47% relative to stagewise deployment on 32 confirmation conditions, at the cost of a 10.19% increase in angular-rate root-mean-square error. In one synthetic computational-fluid-dynamics inflow field, stagewise deployment reduces four-task mean IAE by 2.01% against a same-graph zero-residual control. These simulation results quantify deployment-dependent tracking gains and trade-offs, without establishing general wind rejection or hard-real-time guarantees.
Systems and Control.comment: 25 pages, including supplementary material. Revised title and abstract; clarified the contribution, residual sampling procedure, and discussion. Numerical results unchanged

Systems and Control.title: Local Certificate Repair for Asynchronous Controller Updates in Recommender Systems
Systems and Control.summary: We study how to adapt an existing distributed recommendation controller when local dynamics or objective weights change. Starting from a quadratic stability and cost certificate, we construct positive semidefinite corrections with finite spatial support and an explicit residual. A joint admission test allocates the available dissipation margin to these residuals and to interactions among changes and corrections, including pending updates. The test covers complete declared parameter ranges, allowing different operators to progress independently. For a fixed compatible batch, the corrections define a common storage that guarantees exponential stability and bounds the cost accumulated throughout deployment. When the admitted collection evolves, a reservation protocol preserves the certificate and a rate bound on storage increases ensures exponential convergence. Regional linear-quadratic regulator (LQR) design proposes new gain rows for the operators' own users, and a separate residual-based calculation can certify that the final gain lowers the expected cost. A recommendation-network example illustrates the tradeoff between repair depth, data access, and the benefits of deploying an update.

Systems and Control.title: A complete analytical characterization of optimal collision-free motion for two robots
Systems and Control.summary: Collision-free motion planning for multi-agent robotic systems remains an active research area because of the complexity of coordinating robot trajectories, with applications ranging from coordinated drone shows to autonomous operations on land, in the air, and on water. Importantly, the analytical difficulty of nonconvex collision-avoidance constraints has so far driven the development of exclusively numerical methods. We derive a complete analytical characterization of the optimal trajectories for two robots with zero initial and final velocities, under double-integrator dynamics and a squared-acceleration objective. We prove that these trajectories belong to eight distinct contact families and determine which family applies for each configuration of initial and final positions. We analyze the geometrical properties of the optimal trajectories and provide a numerical algorithm for computing them. These insights have already been adopted to improve the performance of numerical methods for multi-agent motion planning by several orders of magnitude.

Systems and Control.title: Finite-Sample Probabilistic Safety Certification for AI-Based Grid-Edge Coordination
Systems and Control.summary: Coordinating a large population of flexible grid-edge devices can alleviate the need for time-consuming and capital-intensive network upgrades. Artificial intelligence (AI)-based control methods such as multi-agent reinforcement learning or imitation learning are promising to this coordination due to their real-time decision scalability. However, system operators still need an independent and rigorous way to decide whether a given AI system is safe enough for deployment. This paper develops a \emph{finite-sample} probabilistic safety certification framework for AI-based grid-edge coordination. The central idea is to reduce the complete input--AI--decision--evaluation workflow to a binary unsafe outcome under an operator-defined safety specification, and then use exact binomial inference to certify the corresponding unsafe operation probability. Given a set of held-out calibration scenarios, the framework returns the tightest one-sided upper certificate and an accept/reject deployment criterion that controls the probability of false safety certification. Because the certification is for the calibration distribution that may \emph{deviate} from the future operation, we further combine the nominal certificate with physically interpretable sample-space adversarial attacks, a concept widely used in AI models to investigate their fragility. Case studies on grid-edge flexibility coordination with 1{,}000-agent AI models (independent parameters) verify the safety guarantee and the value of integrating adversarial attacks into a rolling-window training-certification-deployment flow.

Systems and Control.title: A Distributed Observer with Random Agent Activations over Random Communication Networks
Systems and Control.summary: This paper develops a distributed observer for the forward-Euler discretization of a continuous-time linear time-invariant system under random local operations and random communications. Under uniform stochastic strong connectivity, we establish almost sure exponential convergence of all local state estimates for sufficiently small discretization step sizes. We further examine how the underlying parameters and components affect the admissible range of the discretization step size and the guaranteed convergence rate bound. Unlike related approaches, the proposed method does not require each local unobservable subspace to admit an $A$-invariant complement.

Systems and Control.title: Over-the-Air Consensus-based Formation Control of Heterogeneous Agents: Communication-Rate and Geometry-Aware Convergence Guarantees
Systems and Control.summary: This paper investigates the formation control problem of heterogeneous, autonomous agents that communicate over a wireless multiple access channel. Instead of avoiding interference through orthogonal node-to-node transmissions, we exploit the superposition property of the wireless channel to compute, at each receiver, normalized convex combinations of simultaneously broadcast neighbor signals. At every communication instant, agents update their reference positions from these aggregates, and track the references in continuous time between updates. The only assumption on the agent dynamics is that each agent tracks constant reference positions exponentially, which accommodates a broad class of platforms. Under this assumption, we analyze the resulting jump-flow system under time-varying communication graphs and unknown channel coefficients. We derive a communication-rate based sufficient condition that guarantees convergence to a prescribed formation. We then provide a geometry-aware refinement showing how favorable tracking transients can relax the required condition. Simulations with unicycle agents illustrate the theoretical results and demonstrate a substantial reduction in the number of required orthogonal transmissions compared to interference-avoiding node-to-node communication protocols.

Systems and Control.title: Scenario-Based Assessment of Transport Electrification for Low-Carbon Urban Planning: A Case Study of Phu Quoc, Vietnam
Systems and Control.summary: Urban net-zero strategies require a defensible emissions boundary and quantitative estimates of the contribution achievable through individual mitigation measures. This study assesses road-transport electrification within a planned residential development in Phu Quoc, Vietnam, using the assumptions and scenario data of an urban-planning study originally prepared in 2022. A vehicle-class inventory combines population-dependent fleet projections, assumed travel activity, gasoline and diesel consumption, fuel-specific carbon dioxide (CO_2) factors, and electricity-related emissions from battery-electric vehicles. The reference case projects annual road-transport emissions of 59.41, 73.86, and 87.23 tCO_2 for 2022, 2025, and 2030, respectively. Three year-specific substitution scenarios, corresponding to nominal electric-vehicle shares of 25%, 50%, and 100%, yield source-reported avoided emissions of 9.43, 13.64, and 55.41 tCO_2/year, or 15.9%, 18.5%, and 63.5% of their respective baselines. However, a cross-scenario audit identifies an inconsistency in the 2025 mixed-fleet results under time-invariant vehicle-class emission-intensity ratios: under that additional assumption, 2025 avoided emissions would be 23.45 rather than 13.64 tCO_2/year. The original detailed vehicle-energy input tables are not included in the available source document, preventing definitive reconciliation. The study therefore provides a transparent, preliminary planning assessment rather than evidence of citywide net-zero attainment. Its principal value is a reproducible accounting structure and an explicit identification of the data, electricity-system, and infrastructure constraints that must be resolved before policy or investment decisions.

Systems and Control.title: Scaling and Trade-offs in Multi-agent Autonomous Systems
Systems and Control.summary: Designing autonomous drone swarms is hampered by a vast design space spanning platform, algorithmic, and numerical-strength choices. We perform large-scale agent-based simulations in three canonical scenarios: swarm-on-swarm battle, cooperative area search with attrition, and pursuit of scattering targets. We demonstrate how dimensional-analysis and data-scaling can be leveraged to collapse performance data onto scaling functions that are mathematically simple, yet counterintuitive and therefore difficult to predict a priori. These scaling laws reveal success-failure boundaries, including sharp break points which we show can be framed as an ``effective swarm size.'' Additionally, we show how this technique can be used to quantify trade-offs between agent count and platform parameters such as velocity, sensing or weapon range, and attrition rate. Furthermore, we show the benefits of embedding an optimal path planning loop within this framework, which can qualitatively improve the scaling laws that govern the outcome. The methods we demonstrate are highly flexible and would enable rapid, budget-aware sizing and algorithm selection for large autonomous swarms.
Systems and Control.comment: Published in Physical Review E. 16 pages, 12 figures

Systems and Control.title: Equilibria and Consensus in Mixed Weighted-Average and Weighted-Median Opinion Dynamics: The Consensus-Promoting Role of Weighted-Average Individuals
Systems and Control.summary: How individuals respond to their neighbors' opinions shapes whether a networked group reaches consensus. This paper analyzes synchronous discrete-time opinion dynamics on a fixed influence network, where individuals use either weighted-average (WA) or weighted-median (WM) opinion-aggregation mechanisms with individual-specific inertia coefficients. We characterize equilibria through graph-theoretic conditions on opinion level sets and WA balance equations, proving that every solution converges to a Lyapunov-stable equilibrium. We define type-dependent cohesive sets, whose WA members assign all their influence weight to the set and WM members assign at least half. The absence of two disjoint such sets gives a necessary and sufficient graph-theoretic criterion for consensus from any initial condition. Otherwise, an open set of initial conditions leads to persistent dissensus. Converting WM individuals to WA cannot create type-dependent cohesive sets and preserves existing guarantees of consensus from any initial condition. If the conversion eliminates every disjoint pair of these sets, the converted system also guarantees consensus from any initial condition. Four numerical studies examine the locations and proportion of weighted-average individuals, as well as the influence weights, while comparing the consensus criterion with finite-horizon simulation outcomes. In the four network ensembles with 100 individuals, the observed frequency of reaching a prescribed consensus tolerance is nondecreasing with WA proportion at each tested simulation horizon. This trend supports the consensus-promoting role of WA individuals, although individual realizations need not follow it.

Signal Processing.title: Karhunen-Loève Transforms of Autoregressive Windows Based on Matched Symmetry Groups
Signal Processing.summary: The Karhunen-Loève transform of a window of a stationary autoregressive process of any order $p$ is described through its poles, extending the Algebraic Diversity framework, which selects a transform by the matched group. For simple roots every basis vector is a sum of at most $p$ sinusoids, at the frequencies where the spectrum equals the eigenvalue, plus modes decaying from the ends. The window covariance differs from a member of the class diagonalized by the type-II discrete cosine transform by a closed-form matrix of rank $2p$, exactly when no pole is zero, so the eigenvalues interlace spectrum samples on the cosine grid, and the coding-gain loss of the cosine transform is an exact function of that matrix with computable bounds: for the $8\times8$ Markov block of image coding at pole $0.95$ it is below 1.2 percent. By Kronecker's theorem the rank is at most $2\max(p,q)$ for rational spectra; a moving-average window departs in its Hankel corners, and an integrated (ARIMA) window departs by low rank from the type-VII sine class, exact for the random walk. The exact symmetry is generically the reflection and contains a wreath product for interleaved windows; the dihedral group of the even extension is matched approximately, the dominant pole's sign choosing cosine or sine. The two groups give the transform a fast form: a parity fold, half-length cosine cores and a cascade of at most $p$ first-order Cauchy stages, exactly $p$ for a minimal AR($p$) model. The first-order case recovers results obtained by other means.
Signal Processing.comment: v1: 38 pages, 7 figures

Signal Processing.title: LWM-TF: A Wireless Foundation Model on 5G NR Time-Frequency Resource Grids
Signal Processing.summary: Received OFDM grids preserve both pilot and payload observations, yet wireless foundation models are rarely pre-trained on them. We introduce LWM-TF, a 9.58M-parameter factorized masked autoencoder pre-trained on complex 5G NR uplink grids taken after the FFT and before channel estimation. Each block attends first across OFDM symbols and then across resource blocks and receive antennas, and the mask follows the same two axes. Because the payload phase is unpredictable, the model reconstructs the normalized log-power of each masked token and predicts its scale separately; ablations show that the two terms are complementary and that this target outperforms complex-signal reconstruction. The encoder is pre-trained on 850,496 physical uplink shared channel (PUSCH) slots from a 10^6-slot dataset simulated with the NR transmit chain under various channel conditions. With the encoder frozen, linear probes classify modulation, predict CRC success, and detect UE mobility. On a separately generated test set, 16 labeled slots per class give 0.85 modulation accuracy, 0.82 CRC area under the ROC curve (AUROC), and 0.73 mobility AUROC, ahead of a supervised CNN on every paired draw. With 10,000 labels the probes reach 0.94, 0.96, and 0.92, well above engineered receiver statistics, and detect mobility where the CNN stays at chance. Without any impairment labels, distances in the frozen feature space flag unseen waveform impairments with 0.78 macro AUROC, against 0.68 for receiver statistics. A single pre-trained encoder thus provides receiver features that transfer across tasks, most strongly when labels are scarce.
Signal Processing.comment: Accepted for publication in IEEE Journal of Selected Topics in Signal Processing (JSTSP)

Signal Processing.title: Descriptor: UWB Anchor Self-Calibration Dataset (UWB-ASC)
Signal Processing.summary: Anchor self-calibration estimates the positions of fixed nodes of an indoor radio positioning or localization system from observations among the nodes and to mobile devices. It replaces the survey of every anchor, which is costly and goes stale when anchors move. The UWB Anchor Self-Calibration Dataset (UWB-ASC) is a testing ground for such methods, recorded in one industrial hall with ultra-wideband (UWB) two-way ranging. It has three parts. The first is two measured deployments. In the line-of-sight (LOS) deployment, 10 anchors range with a walking tag tracked by motion capture. In the non-line-of-sight (NLOS) deployment, 12 nodes range among obstructions, and one of them roves over surveyed markers in 20 quasi-static sessions. Both deployments also hold static sessions, and a total station surveyed every fixed node. The second part is a seeded range simulator that draws synthetic ranges on the surveyed geometry with adjustable error components, from noise-free ranges to NLOS errors, for benchmarks at controlled error levels. Its 81 frozen draws in 5 conditions serve as the reference. The third part is a set of readers that convert the ranges among the static nodes of two public UWB datasets, TWR-CLOUD-Bern and selfloc, into the same format without redistribution. All parts share open Parquet and YAML files, in which topology views select the ranges for each class of calibration method. Raw recordings with rebuild scripts, quality reports, and field labels of the line of sight complete the dataset.

Signal Processing.title: Sample-Efficient Quantum State Tomography for Structured Quantum States in One Dimension
Signal Processing.summary: In this paper, we answer this fundamental question affirmatively by using a class of informationally complete positive operator-valued measures (IC-POVMs), including symmetric IC-POVMs (SIC-POVMs) and spherical $t$-designs, focusing on sample complexity while not accounting for the implementation complexity of the measurement settings. For SIC-POVMs and spherical 2-designs, we show that the number of state copies to guarantee bounded recovery error of an MPO state with a constrained least-squares estimator depends on the probability distribution of the MPO under the POVM but scales only linearly with $n$ when the distribution is approximately uniform. For general spherical $t$-designs with a sufficiently large $t$, we prove that only a number of state copies proportional to the number of independent parameters in the MPO is sufficient for a guaranteed recovery of any state represented by an MPO. In addition, we establish a sample complexity lower bound based on the Cramer-Rao bound, showing that, for strictly positive definite MPO states and unbiased estimators, a number of state copies proportional to the number of independent parameters in the MPO is also necessary, although the upper and lower bounds do not yet match in their dependence on the target accuracy. Furthermore, we propose a spectral method and a projected gradient descent (PGD) algorithm to solve the constrained least-squares problem, both equipped with rigorous recovery error guarantees.

Signal Processing.title: FastSAR: Open-Source SAR Image Formation on CPUs, GPUs, and TPUs, and a Matched Comparison of Algorithms, Precisions, and Processors
Signal Processing.summary: The number of spaceborne synthetic aperture radar (SAR) collectors is growing exponentially, each returning raw collections that must be formed into images. Exact backprojection needs 1.6 trillion interpolated reads and 90 trillion floating-point operations for a 108-megapixel Umbra image. How long it takes to form an image, and at what price, depends on the algorithm, the arithmetic, and the hardware. Open-source implementations have never been compared on matched hardware against a common reference, and none run on Google tensor processing units (TPUs). This paper presents FastSAR, an open-source SAR image formation library for central processing units (CPUs), NVIDIA graphics processing units (GPUs), and TPUs. With it, we compare three SAR image formation algorithms, four floating-point formats, and six cloud devices in every supported combination, with cost per image at on-demand cloud prices as the fair common measure. FastSAR is 1.06 to 22,000 times faster than the tested open-source implementations at equal or better accuracy, and the full suite of hardware, algorithm, and floating-point combinations lets a user choose the Pareto-optimal configuration for their balance of accuracy, speed, and cost. The L4 GPU forms images the cheapest overall. Larger GPUs are faster but cost more per image because their price rises faster than their speed. The TPUs come close to the GPUs in cost, but only for the factorized algorithm, and the CPU is far less efficient in both speed and cost. Lower precision formats buy less of a speedup than expected, and each step down in precision costs accuracy.
Signal Processing.comment: 39 pages, 8 figures. Submitted to IEEE Transactions on Geoscience and Remote Sensing. Code: https://github.com/saulpingerman/FastSAR (pip install fastsar); measurements and paper source: https://github.com/saulpingerman/sar-accel-study

Signal Processing.title: Radiation-Pattern-Based Channel Estimation for Reconfigurable Pixel Antennas
Signal Processing.summary: Reconfigurable pixel antennas provide spatial diversity through multiple radiation patterns generated by a single antenna aperture, but exploiting this diversity can require substantial pilot overhead for exhaustive channel estimation. This paper jointly considers beam-steerable pixel-antenna design and its communication-side channel estimation. A pixel antenna is designed to generate diverse radiation patterns, whose electromagnetic correlation is then exploited to interpolate unobserved channel responses from a limited number of measurements. The proposed approach is evaluated in terms of SNR gain and NMSE, demonstrating that effective pattern selection can be achieved with significantly reduced channel-observation overhead and can even outperform exhaustive scanning at low SNR.

Signal Processing.title: CHANNELS4WORLD: An Environment-Scale Dataset for Wireless Foundation Models
Signal Processing.summary: Wireless foundation models learn reusable representations across tasks, configurations, and deployment environments. Their pretraining requires environmental breadth, yet wireless datasets often sample few sites densely. We introduce Channels4World, a scene-centered dataset of 100,000 distinct outdoor RF scenes and a procedural method for generating them. Each scene links a generated environment and RF material assignments to 32 base-station (BS) positions, 16,384 UE positions, and aligned variable-length multipath and ordered interaction records at 3.5 and 7~GHz. The corpus comprises 52.43 billion physical BS-UE pairs, 104.86 billion frequency-specific evaluations, and a 29.14-TB packaged payload. Scene identity aligns geometry, placements, channels, and interactions across frequencies, allowing environmental breadth and within-scene observation density to vary independently. The public release offers predefined subsets at multiple scales and separate access to corpus components. A deterministic 90K/10K scene-level train-test split keeps both frequencies and all scene components together. We characterize morphology, RF materials, and transceiver placement across three generation profiles. Controlled propagation and path-retention analyses show that diffraction materially affects retained-link availability and multipath structure, while the retention policy reduces storage substantially with little loss in represented aggregate power. Under matched training exposure, models trained on broader scene collections perform better on held-out scenes, although an equal-episode control shows that scene count alone cannot explain the gain. By making environmental breadth explicit and controllable, Channels4World supports the development and evaluation of wireless foundation models for generalization across deployment environments.
Signal Processing.comment: 21 pages, 7 figures, 7 tables

Signal Processing.title: Non-intrusive appliance state detection in unseen homes using classical machine learning
Signal Processing.summary: Non-intrusive load monitoring (NILM) infers, from the aggregate signal of a single smart meter, when each appliance in a home is ON or OFF, offering significant potential to enhance energy efficiency. Classical machine-learning detectors report F1 scores (the harmonic mean of precision and recall) from 0.53 to 0.98, but the causes of this spread are unseparated, so it is unclear which design choices matter. Real-world deployments, however, require detectors that work in houses never seen during training, whereas most studies test on houses used for training. To address this challenge, we propose a factorial analysis of variance design that separates the effects of classifier, feature set and class-imbalance strategy across five appliances (270 configurations), and a leave-house-out protocol with house-grouped model selection. Unlike studies that vary one factor at a time or pool houses, the approach attributes performance to each factor and measures it on unseen homes. Extensive experiments on REFIT, a public dataset of 20 UK households, show that the appliance explains 38 percent of F1 variance, the feature set 13 percent, the classifier 8 percent and the imbalance strategy 2 percent. Pooled testing overstates support-weighted F1 (0.548 versus 0.447 in unseen houses), class weighting gains grow from 32 percent to 69 percent, and feature engineering gives the same 52 percent gain in both protocols. House-grouped selection raises F1 for three of five appliances, by up to 0.110, and a convolutional neural network scores 0.450 (0.496 calibrated) against 0.447 for classical models. The findings guide appliance-level monitoring in smart-metering and energy-management systems.
Signal Processing.comment: 49 pages, 9 figures

Signal Processing.title: Alternating Direction Method of Multipliers for Nonlinear Matrix Decompositions
Signal Processing.summary: We present an algorithm based on the alternating direction method of multipliers (ADMM) for solving nonlinear matrix decompositions (NMD). Given an input matrix $X \in \mathbb{R}^{m \times n}$ and a factorization rank $r \ll \min(m, n)$, NMD seeks matrices $W \in \mathbb{R}^{m \times r}$ and $H \in \mathbb{R}^{r \times n}$ such that $X \approx f(WH)$, where $f$ is an element-wise nonlinear function. We evaluate our method on several representative nonlinear models: the rectified linear unit activation $f(x) = \max(0, x)$, suitable for nonnegative sparse data approximation, the component-wise square $f(x) = x^2$, applicable to probabilistic circuit representation, and the MinMax transform $f(x) = \min(b, \max(a, x))$, relevant for recommender systems. The proposed framework flexibly supports diverse loss functions, including least squares, $\ell_1$ norm, and the Kullback-Leibler divergence, and can be readily extended to other nonlinearities and metrics. We illustrate the applicability, efficiency, and adaptability of the approach on real-world datasets, highlighting its potential for a broad range of applications.
Signal Processing.comment: 54 pages, 7 figures, 6 tables, including supplementary material. Revised version: adds a convergence analysis of the proposed ADMM algorithm (Section S4), a comparison with a dedicated CSF algorithm, and additional experiments. Code available from https://gitlab.com/Atharva05/admm-for-nmd

Signal Processing.title: Energy-Harvesting-Aware Cell-Free LEO Satellite Networks: A Lyapunov Framework for Sustainable User-Centric Beamforming and Clustering
Signal Processing.summary: We study battery-aware downlink control in user-centric cell-free low Earth orbit satellite networks with intermittent solar harvesting and finite onboard batteries. A perturbed Lyapunov controller coordinates clustering and hybrid beamforming using measured battery states and causal harvest forecasts. The per-slot solver combines group-sparse association, rate bounds, a quadratic transform, and successive convex approximation. We establish robust battery invariance for feasible implemented actions and give a utility bound conditional on a comparison policy and the per-slot implementation gap. Multi-orbit control-layer simulations show that queue-aware scheduling preserves a larger battery reserve in the stressed scenario at the expense of effective energy efficiency. A separate fixed-cluster matrix snapshot illustrates recovered hybrid beam patterns and the per-slot objective trace.

Signal Processing.title: WiFo-R: Wireless Foundation Model with Recurrent Channel Representation
Signal Processing.summary: Wireless foundation models learn transferable channel state information (CSI) representations across heterogeneous wireless systems. However, conventional grid-aligned representations couple feature sequence length to CSI dimensions, restricting the allocation of representation capacity to different propagation conditions and task requirements while increasing inference overhead. This paper proposes WiFo-R, a wireless foundation model that learns progressive channel representations with selectable capacity. A channel-query cross-attention encoder aggregates spatial, temporal, and spectral CSI information, while parameter-shared recurrent updates refine existing channel features and introduce additional latent tokens. Multi-mask, multi-depth self-supervised pretraining equips intermediate states with strong reconstruction capabilities, followed by task-aligned post-training for channel estimation and CSI feedback. WiFo-R supports temporal and frequency-domain channel prediction, channel estimation, and variable-rate CSI feedback, and transfers to localization and LoS/NLoS classification. Experiments across in-distribution and out-of-distribution channel configurations demonstrate accurate reconstruction, progressive performance improvements, and strong transferability. A single feedback encoder--decoder supports six payload lengths at fixed quantization precision, while cross-attention and selectable recurrent depth improve the accuracy--complexity trade-off for large-scale CSI observations.

Signal Processing.title: Nonlinear Interference Estimation in Coherent Optical Systems: Principles and Applications
Signal Processing.summary: Accurate estimation of nonlinear interference (NLI) is important for monitoring and optimizing coherent optical networks. This invited paper reviews the main techniques proposed for receiver-side NLI estimation, with particular focus on longitudinal power monitoring (LPM). We discuss the principles, advantages and limitations of LPM-based NLI estimation, including recent experimental demonstrations. We then experimentally investigate the impact of the spatial step size and the number of averaged constellation blocks on estimation accuracy. The results show that accurate NLI estimation does not necessarily require a highly accurate power profile, with limited improvements obtained by increasing the number of averaged blocks. Finally, we discuss the main practical limitations and applications of NLI estimation, with particular attention to end-to-end and span-wise optical power optimization.
Signal Processing.comment: 10 pages, 7 figures. Extended version of an invited talk at ECOC 2026. Submitted to the Journal of Lightwave Technology

Signal Processing.title: Synergizing CKM and ISAC for Environment-Aware Wireless Networks
Signal Processing.summary: Channel knowledge map (CKM) and integrated sensing and communications (ISAC) have emerged as two key technologies for sixth-generation (6G) and beyond wireless networks, enabling a new paradigm toward environment-aware system design. CKMs provide static or stochastic wireless environment information a priori by learning location-dependent mappings from transceiver positions to channel knowledge of various types, whereas ISAC exploits wireless signals to sense environmental objects in real time. CKM and ISAC have primarily been studied separately in prior works, while their integration offers a promising approach for enhancing the environment awareness of 6G networks and further improving both sensing and communication capabilities. On the one hand, sensing can support CKM construction by providing location-tagged measurements and richer environmental observations, while also enabling real-time CKM refinement in dynamic environments. On the other hand, CKM can enhance sensing by offering prior environmental information for clutter mitigation, and CKM and sensing information can be jointly leveraged to improve communications. This article provides an overview of the complementary interactions between CKMs and ISAC, with particular emphasis on three design approaches: sensing-assisted CKM construction and refinement, CKM-assisted sensing, and joint CKM- and sensing-enhanced communications. We also discuss future research directions for achieving environment-aware wireless networks.

Signal Processing.title: A Multi-View Low-Latency Direction-Sensing for Low-Altitude Network via a Multi-Armed Array
Signal Processing.summary: Due to the directional antenna pattern, the received signal power decreases when the target deviates from the array boresight, degrading direction-sensing accuracy. Although rotatable arrays can alleviate this problem, repeated array rotations will induce an incremental long sensing latency. To break the dilemma of harvesting the directive gain from element and making a low-latency sensing, a multi-armed array comprising multiple subarrays with different orientations is proposed to provide wide spatial coverage encompassing low-altitude and terrestrial regions while enabling multi-view direction sensing. However, the different views lead to different direction-sensing accuracies. To fully exploit the complementary information from multiple views, two fusion methods, called SNR-weighted fusion and logistic-weighted fusion, are developed. The former directly assigns fusion weights according to the estimated received SNRs, whereas the latter employs an exponential SNR mapping to further emphasize high-SNR subarrays. Furthermore, the Cramer-Rao lower bound (CRLB) is derived to provide a theoretical benchmark for the proposed multi-view direction-sensing system. Simulation results show that logistic-weighted fusion achieves better accuracy in the very low-SNR regime, while both proposed methods approach the CRLB at medium and high SNRs and maintain stable sensing performance.

Signal Processing.title: PPG2ECG: Physiology-Guided Latent Rectified Flow for Electro-Hemodynamic PPG-to-ECG Generation
Signal Processing.summary: Electrocardiography (ECG) is the clinical standard for cardiac assessment but requires dedicated hardware that does not scale to daily-life monitoring. Photoplethysmography (PPG) is ubiquitous in wearables but lacks ECG-specific diagnostic morphology and is corrupted by motion and sensor noise. PPG-to-ECG generation aims to bridge this gap by recovering electrical morphology and timing from peripheral pulse signals. However, existing methods largely rely on statistical alignment and data-driven generation. They fail to explicitly structure the latent space around physiology-aware electro-hemodynamic factors and lack constraints from forward physiological dynamics. To address these challenges, we propose PPG2ECG, a physiology-guided latent rectified flow framework. PPG2ECG introduces an electro-hemodynamic simulator that co-models ECG and PPG through shared cardiac phase dynamics. Guided by this simulator, a Physiology-Aware AutoEncoder learns a structured electro-hemodynamic latent space. Then we integrate this simulator guidance into a PPG-conditioned latent rectified flow, enforcing ECG-side morphology consistency and ECG-to-PPG forward hemodynamic consistency during generative transport. Experiments on the large-scale MC-MED dataset demonstrate that PPG2ECG significantly improves PPG-to-ECG generation and downstream cardiovascular disease classification, proving its ability to generate ECGs that are both signal-faithful and physiologically plausible under the ECG-to-PPG hemodynamic pathway
Signal Processing.comment: Accepted to NeurIPS 2026

Signal Processing.title: Image Steganography For Securing Intellicise Wireless Networks: "Invisible Encryption" Against Eavesdroppers
Signal Processing.summary: As one of the most promising technologies for intellicise (intelligent and consice) wireless networks, Semantic Communication (SemCom) significantly improves communication efficiency by extracting, transmitting, and recovering semantic information, while reducing transmission delay. However, an integration of communication and artificial intelligence (AI) also exposes SemCom to security and privacy threats posed by intelligent eavesdroppers. To address this challenge, image steganography in SemCom embeds secret semantic features within cover semantic features, allowing intelligent eavesdroppers to decode only the cover image. This technique offers a form of "invisible encryption" for SemCom. Motivated by these advancements, this paper conducts a comprehensive exploration of integrating image steganography into SemCom. Firstly, we assess the potential of image steganography in enhancing the security of SemCom. Secondly, we delve into traditional and DL-based image steganographic paradigms for securing SemCom. Thirdly, we further discuss six image semantic steganography strategies. Fourthly, we present a case study to illustrate the effectiveness of coverless steganography SemCom. Finally, we propose future research directions for image steganography SemCom.
Signal Processing.comment: 8 pages, 5 figures

Signal Processing.title: An In-Ear Sleep Modulation SoC Featuring a CNN-LSTM Accelerator with Long-Kernel Memory Reuse and Runtime Dynamic Quantization
Signal Processing.summary: This work presents a 65 nm SoC for closed-loop in-ear sleep modulation. The SoC performs low-noise in-ear EEG sensing, CNN-LSTM-based sleep stage classification, and phase-specific auditory stimulation under 1 mW. A dedicated accelerator is developed, featuring a memory reuse technique to efficiently process long kernels required for low-frequency EEG feature extraction. A runtime dynamic quantization is incorporated, reducing model size by 3.88 times with only a 0.28% loss in accuracy. A sensitivity of 98.3% is achieved for deep sleep detection, enabling effective sleep modulation.
Signal Processing.comment: Author accepted manuscript. 4 pages, including a one-page copyright and publication information cover sheet. Published in the 2026 IEEE/JSAP Symposium on VLSI Technology and Circuits. Yaqian Xu and Xinyu Chen contributed equally

Signal Processing.title: Analysis of the Effect of Doppler on Direct-to-Cell: Real-World Performance and Proposed Improvements
Signal Processing.summary: Direct-to-cell (DtC) satellites serve unmodified LTE phones today from low Earth orbit, where the satellite's motion creates Doppler shifts of tens of kHz. Since large offsets such as these cannot be compensated adequately by the user equipment (UE), the satellite pre-compensates the Doppler shift of each beam, but it can do so for only one reference point in the beam. A UE elsewhere in the beam still has to compensate a residual offset; previous field studies report residuals of up to 10 kHz, beyond the $\pm$7.5 kHz that the 15 kHz subcarrier spacing can resolve. In this paper we corroborate this effect with our own detailed measurements of Starlink transmissions and further correlate ineffective handover performance to inadequate residual offset compensation. We analyze the Doppler compensation problem with detailed standard-specific simulations and propose a compensation method at the UE, based on the location of the UE with respect to the beam reference point used for the Doppler compensation and the known satellite location, that improves the efficiency of handover. With UE cell-specific pre-compensation, the neighbors are identified, read correctly and handed over to in time rather than lost to radio-link failure.

Computer Science and Game Theory.title: Homological Barriers to Stable Learning of First-Order Nash Equilibria
Computer Science and Game Theory.summary: We identify a homological barrier to stable learning of local Nash equilibria, also known as first-order Nash equilibria (FONE), in constrained non-concave differentiable games. We consider continuous deterministic learning dynamics that fix every FONE point and aim to attract all initial conditions to the full FONE set. We show that this convergence guarantee is impossible when the target set has nontrivial positive-degree cohomology, such as that arising from a loop, and the state space is compact and contractible. We exhibit this barrier in a simple non-concave quadratic zero-sum game on a box whose exact FONE set consists of a diagonal six-edge loop and an isolated point. Consequently, no such dynamics can make the full FONE set a stable global attractor. We further show that degree two is the minimal polynomial degree at which this barrier can arise and extend the construction to obtain nontrivial homology in arbitrarily high degrees. Finally, we establish that the barrier persists for sufficiently small approximate-FONE targets under small perturbations, yielding an open, positive-volume family of quadratic zero-sum games with the same homological barrier.
Computer Science and Game Theory.comment: The Fortieth Annual Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems (NeurIPS) 2026
